record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: Can a portable, fast, lightweight, flexible on-device runtime be built for federated learning so that end-user devices can serialize, receive, interpret or execute, and communicate machine-learning training computations without the limitations of large or unstable framework-specific runtimes?

evidence.quote: no solution exists yet that satisfies these requirements

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Design and demonstrate a portable, lightweight, and flexible on-device runtime system for federated learning with the following properties. The runtime must execute on heterogeneous end-user devices (e.g., mobile phones, embedded devices, browsers) with limited memory, compute, and energy budgets, and must support the full federated training loop, namely: (i) receiving from a server a serialized description of a machine-learning training computation (including model architecture, loss, optimizer step, and any client-side data-processing pipeline), (ii) deserializing and interpreting or executing that computation on locally held data to produce model updates, and (iii) communicating the resulting updates back to the server in a serialized form. The runtime should satisfy simultaneously:

1. Portability: a single runtime binary or specification that runs across major device platforms without per-platform reimplementation of the training logic.
2. Small footprint: binary size and memory usage substantially smaller than full-fledged machine-learning framework runtimes designed for datacenter use.
3. Stability: deterministic and reliable execution suitable for deployment to large populations of consumer devices.
4. Expressivity / flexibility: ability to represent and execute a broad class of model architectures, optimizers, and training procedures (not a fixed model family), with the computation specified by the server rather than hard-coded into the client.
5. Efficiency: training throughput on-device competitive with native implementations of the same computation.

Construct such a runtime, together with a serialization format for training computations and a precise specification of the supported class of computations, and prove (empirically and via formal guarantees on the serialization/execution semantics) that all of the above properties are met simultaneously; or, alternatively, establish an impossibility result showing that some subset of these requirements cannot be satisfied together under reasonable assumptions on device capabilities.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is framed as an open systems challenge in federated learning. While various lightweight on-device ML runtimes (e.g., TensorFlow Lite, ExecuTorch, ONNX Runtime Mobile, Flower client, PyTorch Mobile) provide partial solutions—mostly for inference and limited on-device training—no single runtime is widely recognized as satisfying all of the portability, footprint, stability, flexibility, and efficiency requirements for arbitrary server-specified federated training computations. The problem appears to remain open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Lists building portable, lightweight on-device runtimes for FL as an open problem; states no solution yet meets all stated requirements.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as open in the federated learning open-problems literature.

status_evidence.title: ExecuTorch / PyTorch Edge
status_evidence.snippet: On-device runtime supporting inference and limited training on edge devices.
status_evidence.claim: Partial solutions exist but do not yet meet the full set of requirements for federated training.
